Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

Changes in version 0.6.0

Continuous tracking of cycles with uncertainty

  • New track_ridge_hmm(): continuous tracking of one cycle through any scalogram (wavelet, synchrosqueezed, superlet-SST, ConceFT) with a hidden Markov model (forward-backward and Viterbi): bridges gaps of sharp scalograms, gives a credible band, a confidence curve and, with period_of_tracked_cycle, the sedimentation rate and an age model with uncertainty from posterior paths. The output works with curve2time().
  • New track_astro_hmm(): astronomically constrained tracking of the sedimentation rate using all cycles together (eccentricity, obliquity, precession; periods and weights adjustable for deep time), optionally inside a rough guide. In synthetic tests (2000 kyr, changing sedimentation rate, AR1 noise) the age model from analyse_superlet_sst() + track_astro_hmm() was within 3-20 kyr at the end of the record (maximum error 8-25 kyr), against 55-120 kyr for picking the maximum in a band.
  • track_ridge_hmm() and track_astro_hmm() accept jump_depths (known hiatuses or abrupt facies changes, where abrupt changes of the sedimentation rate are allowed) and track_astro_hmm() background = "ar1". Stress tests with three jumps of the sedimentation rate and AR1 noise: largest age error about 2 % of the duration (noise half the signal), 3-4 % (noise equal to the signal), 6-9 % (noise twice the signal), about half of the error of picking the strongest power in a band; with noise three times the signal only with a rough guide (about 7 %). At high noise the credible bands are too narrow when the track follows the wrong cycle.
  • New track_astro_auto(): the recommended workflow in one call (scalogram that keeps weak cycles, astronomically constrained tracking with deep-time periods, optional guide and jump depths) plus an independent long-window (eCOCO-like) estimate of the sedimentation rate; intervals where the two disagree or the confidence is low are flagged. In stress tests (3000 kyr, three jumps, AR1 noise) the largest age error was 32-44 kyr (noise half the signal), 67-78 kyr (equal), about 190 kyr (twice, MSST scalogram); with noise three times the signal the track failed, but the flags covered about 90 % of the wrong intervals.
  • New astro_periods_tracking(): eccentricity, obliquity and precession periods with weights for any age (AstroGeo22 precession constant via astro_terms()) or a given k, e.g. for Silurian/Devonian records; track_astro_hmm() gained age_ma, k_yr, long_weight, local_weight and guide_penalty.
  • New plot_track() (with show and flags).
  • track_astro_hmm(): consistent_cycles = TRUE (default) uses only the cycles that stay inside the resolved period range over the whole sedimentation-rate range (before, rates that moved more cycles into the range were favoured, e.g. the ~110-kyr cycle read as obliquity in the eccentricity-only Klonk record); track_astro_auto() no longer drops the 405-kyr cycle at the top of the sedimentation-rate range.
  • Tests on six real records (ODP 1119; Orcadian Basin 12/13-1; KTG-01; Klonk; Bisciaro; Pod Barrandovem) led to: evidence normalised by a running median along the period axis (normalise = "median", removes the red-noise bias), cycles outside the resolved period range no longer favoured, duration argument of track_astro_auto() (approximate duration as a wide prior on the mean sedimentation rate; without such a prior the tracks were often a factor ~2 off, with it the durations agreed within ~15 % with the published or manual age models in 9 of 12 runs), flags from the spread of the posterior (confidence10) instead of the long-window estimate, and time_median (posterior median age) in the output.

Even more wavelets, higher-order and superlet synchrosqueezing

  • 11 further wavelet families (22 in total): exactly zero-mean Morlet ("morlet0"), real Morlet ("morl"), Hermitian hat ("hhat"), Poisson, gammatone, Hann (raised cosine), and the orthogonal Haar, Daubechies ("db1"-"db20"), Symlets ("sym2"-"sym20") and Battle-Lemarie spline wavelets, computed in the frequency domain from their filters (Daubechies and Symlet filters by spectral factorisation). PyWavelets style names ("db4", "sym8", "cgau3", "gaus2", "cmor1.5-1", "shan2-1.5", "fbsp2-1-1.5") are accepted, and wavelet can be a user defined function psi_hat(omega).
  • analyse_wavelet_sst(): sst_order = 2 (second-order synchrosqueezing, Oberlin et al. 2015, 2017) corrects the instantaneous frequency for the chirp rate, so ridges follow fast changes of the sedimentation rate also with long wavelets; type = "set" (synchroextracting transform, Yu et al. 2017); several omega_nr values give adaptive synchrosqueezing (per position the wavelet with the lowest Renyi entropy, Sheu et al. 2017).
  • analyse_wavelet_sst() also gained n_iter (multisynchrosqueezing, Yu et al. 2019: the frequency reassignment is repeated) and type = "reassign" (reassigned scalogram, Auger and Flandrin 1995: power moved in period and in depth/time).
  • New analyse_superlet_sst(): synchrosqueezed transforms of wavelets with an increasing number of cycles (default omega_0 = 8, 12, 16; second order, 4 reassignment iterations) combined by their geometric mean (superlet principle, Moca et al. 2021). In synthetic tests (eccentricity-modulated precession and obliquity, changing sedimentation rate, AR1 noise) it put 75-90 % of the energy within 3 % of the true periods, against 25-40 % for the Morlet scalogram, and separated the 19 and 23.7 kyr precession bands best.
  • New analyse_conceft(): ConceFT multitaper synchrosqueezing with orthonormal generalised Morse wavelets (Daubechies, Wang and Wu 2016), and method = "multitaper".
  • New sst_significance(): significance of synchrosqueezed transforms against AR noise (optionally with a changing variance) by simulation with the same settings; non-significant coefficients are removed.

More wavelets, wavelet agnostic functions, SST defaults, FFT uncertainty

  • analyse_wavelet() now offers 11 mother wavelets: Morlet, Paul, DOG (Mexican hat = order 2), Morse, bump, complex Morlet ("cmor"), analytic Gaussian derivative ("cgau"), Shannon, frequency B-spline ("fbsp"), Meyer and log-Gabor; with aliases ("gabor", "mexh", "ricker", "gmw", "cauchy", …).
  • analyse_Xwavelet(), analyse_wavelet_coherence(), analyse_Awavelet(), analyse_superlet() and analyse_Xsuperlet() gained wavelet and wavelet_order. In the adaptive wavelet and the superlets the number of cycles is converted to the Morlet equivalent bandwidth of the chosen wavelet; the Morlet results are numerically unchanged.
  • analyse_wavelet_sst() works with every analytic wavelet (all except DOG). Default omega_nr = 12, noise threshold "riskshrink" (universal threshold on the finest scales), amplitude linear colour levels in plots.
  • New fft_frequency_uncertainty() (practical 1/T and Heisenberg-Gabor 1/(4 pi T) frequency uncertainty, relative uncertainty) and fft_uncertainty() (uncertainty of a tracked cycle and its time model, Fourier counterpart of wavelet_uncertainty()).

Wavelets * analyse_wavelet() has new arguments wavelet and wavelet_order: besides the Morlet wavelet (default, unchanged) the Paul, derivative-of-Gaussian (DOG, e.g. Mexican hat), generalised Morse and bump wavelets can be used. The period axis is always the Fourier period. The reconstruction constant and the cone of influence follow the wavelet, so extract_signal*(), wavelet_significance() and the plotting functions work with the new wavelets. The cross-wavelet, coherence and Awavelet functions are still Morlet only. * New analyse_wavelet_sst() (alias analyze_wavelet_sst()): wavelet synchrosqueezing transform (Daubechies et al. 2011; Thakur et al. 2013). The result has the structure of analyse_wavelet(), so plot_wavelet(), tracking and extraction work on it; ridges of cycles are much thinner and the transform stays invertible.

New functions * mesa_spectrum() and plot_mesa_spectrum(): maximum entropy spectral analysis (MESA, Burg). Burg recursion in base R (identical coefficients to stats::ar.burg), AR order chosen with FPE, AIC, MDL or CAT or set by hand, one-sided power spectral density with the variance preserved, and peak table with prominence. * mesa_evolutive(), track_mesa(), mesa_average() and plot_mesa_evolutive(): evolutive MESA with one or several window lengths (for example 30, 40 and 50 m), padding of the window at the top and bottom (pad) so that the spectrum spans the entire record, peak extraction at every window position, dynamic-programming tracking of a spectral ridge, average amplitude spectrum, and spectral-image plot. mesa_spectrum() also accepts a single window with padding. * test_tuned(), plot_test_k() and test_tuned_check(): updated precession-constant test for tuned records (version 3). MTM peaks (optionally of several proxies pooled) are assigned to k+s3, k+s6, k+g5, k+g2 and k+g4 over a wide k range (default 19.5-23.5 kyr) instead of windows around AstroGeo22, with a pre-scan that removes intervals with little precession, ambiguity handling of peak assignments, combined k with uncertainty, an Earth-Moon distance and length-of-day conversion, and two further tests (spectral peaks, amplitude modulation against surrogates). Works better for Silurian/Devonian data.

British English * WaverideR now uses British spelling as its primary spelling: analyse_wavelet(), analyse_superlet(), analyse_Awavelet(), analyse_Xwavelet(), analyse_Xsuperlet(), analyse_wavelet_coherence() and wr_coloured_noise(). The American names (analyze_*, wr_colored_noise()) remain available as identical aliases that share the same help page. Arguments with American spelling also accept British synonyms (colour_brewer, colour_grid, standardise, centre_limits, normalise); the original argument names keep working.

Removed (overlap with ‘astrochron’) * berger_periods() removed (overlaps with astrochron::bergerPeriods()); compare_published() no longer contains the Berger et al. row and the data file Berger1989Periods.txt was removed. * Hilbert_transform() is no longer exported; use astrochron::hilbert(). A padded internal helper is still used by extract_amplitude().

Parallel computing * foreach/doSNOW replaced by an internal base-R parallel helper. Sequential by default; run_multicore = TRUE plus the new n_cores argument switch parallel on. Cores are capped (physical cores - 1, max 4, tasks, free RAM, CRAN limit) and work is done in batches with incremental combining so memory stays bounded. Results are reproducible with set.seed() and independent of the number of cores. * Forked workers on Linux/macOS, PSOCK workers on Windows and in RStudio (WaverideR must be installed for PSOCK workers).

Plot windows * New wr_open_device(): no more Windows-only code. Interactive tracking (identify()) works on Windows, macOS (XQuartz/Quartz) and Linux (X11) and gives a clear message when no interactive device is available. * dev_new now defaults to TRUE only in the RStudio GUI (separate window needed for raster plots); override with options(waverider.dev_new = ...).

Integrated functions * All acycle2R functions (astrochronology, Earth-Moon, COCO/eCOCO, etc.), with data in inst/extdata. * astroMCBchron() and modBchron() with print/summary/predict/plot methods and a memory guard.

Dependencies * Removed: foreach, doSNOW, DescTools, Hmisc, Matrix, matrixStats, reshape2, truncnorm, colorednoise, trapezoid, fANCOVA, DecomposeR, rlist, RColorBrewer, colorRamps, viridis (base-R replacements). scico and magick are now optional (Suggests).

Fixes * track_ecoco(): new interactive tracker for eCOCO results, the counterpart of track_period(). Plot the eCOCO map (pcoco, rho, …), click ridge points (click again to deselect) and get the tracked sedimentation rate against depth. Points can also be given as a table (points =) for scripted, reproducible tracking, and the result can be interpolated to all windows. * analyze_superlet() was checked against a direct convolution implementation of Moca et al. (2021) and corrected: (1) the default settings and order_scaling = "none" multiplied the order by c1 (and o = NULL used order c1 instead of 1); (2) order_scaling = "power" used the wrong operator precedence and "quadratic" was documented but missing; (3) records with a non-zero mean or a trend (typical for stratigraphic proxies) gave power at the longest periods and large edge effects, so a linear trend (or mean) is now removed and the record standardised (detrend, standardize; use detrend = "none", standardize = FALSE for the old behaviour); (4) amplitudes are computed from sums of logarithms (no underflow for high orders) and phases as circular means; (5) a phase sign convention that was opposite to analyze_wavelet(); (6) new output coi (cone of influence) and order, and a warning when lowerPeriod is below the Nyquist period. (7) the additive cycle rule (mult = FALSE) is now checked against Moca et al. (2021): the i-th wavelet has c1 + i - 1 cycles (it was c1 + i, so order 1 differed from the multiplicative case); additive results change accordingly. * analyze_Xsuperlet(): order_scaling and order_alpha were not passed on to analyze_superlet(); the default upperPeriod/lowerPeriod values were swapped; the cross spectrum was divided by the period although superlet amplitudes are not scale dependent; the cross phase was taken from a complex geometric mean, whose phase is not defined (it wraps), and is now the difference of the circular-mean phases. Records are now trimmed to their common, complete part. * New wavelet_significance(): significance levels for wavelet and superlet scalograms. method = "analytic" is the instantaneous Torrence and Compo (1998) red-noise test (local chi-square levels and the global spectrum with its degrees of freedom; wavelets only; about 4-5 percent false positives in simulations with Morlet omega 6, 8 and 10). method = "surrogate" runs noise surrogates through the same transform (wavelets and superlets) with white, AR(1), signal-corrected AR(1) (candidate periods removed before the noise is estimated) or power-law backgrounds, gives the scale-wise 95 percent level outside the cone of influence and the global spectrum level (after the Weesp analysis), and optionally p-values for candidate cycles. Surrogates run on several cores with results independent of the number of cores. plot_wavelet() and plot_superlet() have the new argument add_signif to outline the significant cells and draw the global level. * New wavelet_band_significance(): significance of the scale-averaged wavelet power (Torrence and Compo 1998, section 4d) over a period band such as the obliquity or precession band, against a white or AR(1) background, instantaneous and only at points where the whole band lies outside the cone of influence. method = "exact" (default) derives the null distribution from the eigenvalues of the band-averaged quadratic form, so it is valid for any omega_nr, dj, band and background (checked against Monte Carlo and 4.6-5.1 percent false positives for omega 4, 6, 10 and 12). method = "torrence" is the published chi-square form; its constant (decorrelation length 0.60) only holds for omega 6 and makes the test too conservative for larger omega (about 2 percent false positives at omega 10), so it is rescaled to 0.6 * 6 / omega_nr by default. Includes print and plot methods. * The scalogram plots (plot_wavelet(), plot_Awavelet(), plot_eha_log2(), plot_superlet(), plot_Xwavelet(), plot_Xsuperlet(), plot_wavelet_coherence()) now share one set of panel functions (R/plot_wavelet_panels.R) instead of 8 to 16 hand-copied layout branches each: the seven files shrank from about 17,700 to about 2,000 lines (plus 400 lines of shared panels), and the colour palette code that was copied into 17 functions is one helper. The output was checked pixel by pixel against the previous version for several hundred option combinations (data, average, MTM panels, horizontal/vertical, direction, period limits, lines, points, ablines, p-values, significance contours, arrows); it is identical except for the bug fixes below. * Plot bug fixes found while doing this: color_brewer = "viridis" and "colorRamps" failed in several plot functions (a stray space in the generated function name); the heat.colors, terrain.colors, topo.colors and cm.colors palettes failed (they have no start/end arguments); analyze_wavelet(pval = TRUE) stopped with an error; plot_eha_log2(plot_opt = "Power") used a non-existing field for the average; the vertical plot_eha_log2() layout without extra panels drew no period axis, frame or user lines; the vertical plot_Xwavelet() layout with data panel and no average failed; the cross spectrum and superlet plots with data and average panels drew a stray y axis in the global spectrum panel; p-value overlays redrew axes. plot_eha_log2() and analyze_wavelet() lost their large commented-out old copies. * analyze_superlet(): the cone of influence followed the integer order of the widest wavelet and therefore had steps; it now follows the fractional order and is smooth. The wavelets are made per frequency instead of all being kept in memory, which lowers the memory use for long records, and run_multicore/n_cores compute the frequencies on several cores (identical results). The object also stores mult, detrend and standardize. * flmw() accepts superlet objects. * plot_superlet(), plot_Xsuperlet() and track_period() now shade the cone of influence of superlet objects (coi.1, coi.2), in both orientations, as for wavelets. * flmw(): classic method rewritten with vectorised code, about 50-60 times faster with identical output (checked against the previous version, including run_random = TRUE). The old code stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” for some spectra; this no longer happens. New arguments method (“classic”, “weighted”, “template”), tolerance and whiten; results gain score_mat and best_sedrate. * New flmw_path(): continuity along depth (Viterbi path) and posterior probabilities with credible intervals, optional sedimentation rate bounds and hiatuses. In a synthetic test (6 cycles, noise equal to the signal, sedimentation rate changing 3-6 cm/kyr) the root mean square error fell from about 2.0 cm/kyr (classic, best score per depth) to about 0.15-0.2 cm/kyr (template or weighted score plus path). * model_red_noise_wt() computes the Morlet wavelets once and transforms all scales with one mvfft() call (about 2 to 4 times faster, identical output). sum_power_sedrate() is rewritten without per-position loops over data frames: band limits and local maxima are computed once and window maxima come from a sparse table, about 20 times faster with identical output (checked on several settings). * wavelet_significance(): the critical level of the global spectrum was NA (red dashed line stopped) at periods without any point outside the cone of influence, while the global spectrum itself was drawn there. The analytic level now uses the instantaneous level (2 degrees of freedom) there and the surrogate level uses all points, so the line is continuous over the whole period range; gws (observed) is still NA there. * Found with a plot gallery of all examples and layouts: plot_eha_log2() failed when lowerPeriod/upperPeriod were not given (it looked for a non-existing $Period; they now default to the range of the object). The phase arrows of plot_Xwavelet(), plot_Xsuperlet() and plot_wavelet_coherence() had fixed lengths in depth and period units (T_unit = 15, P_unit = 0.5), which is far too large for short records and distorts the angle; the default is now automatic (T_unit = NULL, P_unit = NULL: 0.3 inch whatever the record length, with the screen angle equal to the phase angle). Colour key labels no longer repeat (0.001, 0.001, 0.000) for small powers, and the p-value axis of the global spectrum no longer collides with the colour key. * analyze_superlet(): the left and right cone-of-influence polygons overlapped (darker band, crossing lines) at long periods, where the edge zones are wider than half the record. The cone of influence is now one polygon, whose sides meet in the middle of the record like the dome of the wavelet plots (coi itself is unchanged). * plot_astro_anchor(): the example used time_dir = FALSE for anchor points in which time increases with depth, so all tie lines crossed in one point; it now uses time_dir = TRUE (set time_dir = FALSE only for sections where time decreases with depth). * New astro_anchor_interactive(): a more flexible version of astro_anchor(). Proxy record and astronomical solution are shown together with their peaks; tie points are set by clicking a peak in each record (in either order, in any place of the record), removed by clicking a tied peak again, and the windows can be zoomed and moved. Tune and inspect opens a second window at any moment with the record tuned to the current tie points, a cycle extracted from it, the astronomical solution (with the correlation) and the sedimentation rate between the tie points; tie points in the wrong order are flagged. Tie lines connect the points in both windows; partners outside the other window are shown as stubs with their position, and Sync moves one window to the partners of the tie points in the other. The result has the same columns as astro_anchor(). Existing tie points can be passed in ties, and locator_fun allows scripted use. * New astro_anchor_app(): a Shiny app (runs locally) for tying a proxy record to an astronomical solution. Proxy record, astronomical solution and the record tuned to the current tie points (with an extracted cycle, the astronomical solution and the sedimentation rate) are shown in one window, joined by numbered tie lines, and update while tie points are made, selected, moved, untied (double click) and undone. Astronomical tie points always sit on a maximum/minimum; proxy tie points can be placed on the raw record or on a cycle extracted with a Taner filter (flow, fhigh, roll = 10^x), need not lie on peaks, and can be moved with fine/coarse buttons, by typing a position or an offset from the nearest peak, by clicking or by dragging. The astronomical target can be a provided solution (or a list of them), a metronome (cosine with chosen period, phase and interval) or a Laskar solution (La2004 ETP/eccentricity/obliquity/precession, La2010a-d, La2011, insolation; downloaded on request) over a chosen time interval. Both records have window sliders, number boxes, mouse-wheel zoom and Shift+drag panning, and both axes can be flipped and the time direction reversed (reference frame). Needs the suggested package shiny. * add_MTM = TRUE in plot_wavelet() (“object ‘MTM_res_1’ not found”) is covered by a regression test. * retrack_wt_MC(): duplicated sequential branch removed. * Random draws from truncated normals use an inverse-CDF method and are not bit-identical to earlier versions for a given seed.

Changes in version 0.3.2

CRAN release: 2023-09-06

added functions:

add_wavelet adds a wavelet plot to a larger plot

add_wavelet_avg adds the average wavelet power to a larger plot

curve2time_unc converts a tracked period curve to time taking the uncertainty of the curve into account

curve2time_unc_anchor converts a tracked period curve to time by taking the uncertainty of the curve and anchored radiometric date into account

dur_gaps calculates the duration off a hiatus based on the missing part of an astronomical cycle

geo_col generate standard color codes for the Geological Time Scale

geo_loc generates ages for the boundaries of a geochronological subdivision

geo_mid generate the mean age of a geological subdivision

lithlog_disc discriticizes lithologs from a block pattern to a continous signal which allows it to analyzed using spectral analysis techniques

minimal_tuning Creates an age model using the minimal tuning technique. This means that the distance between 2 peaks of an extracted cycle is set to duration of the interpreted astronomical cycle

retrack_wt_MC Re-track cycles using a Monte-Carlo simulation Then input is an already tracked period of an astronomical cycle and the wavelet in which it was tracked. the already tracked periods are combined to create a pseudo-curve which is then re-tracked in one of the wavelets (randomly selected) the result is a bunch of retracked curves

sedrate2tune converts a data set using the sedimentation rate to a tuned age-model

updated functions:

Hilbert_transform added side padding to avoid edge effects

plot_wavelet added additional color plotting option

plot_win_fft added additional color plotting option

track_period_wavelet added additional color plotting option added the option to select any point within the plot

Changes in version 0.3.1

CRAN release: 2023-06-22

Examples contained dontrun{} which were replaced with donttest{} when examples are executed in >5 seconds otherwise dontrun{} is removed completely. Searched all files using CTR:+SHIFT+F to see if dontrun{} was still present and dontrun{} was not found after replacement

Checked and can now confirm that only 1 core is used by default in functions which can run using multiple cores by default the parameter to run multiple cores is set to (run_multicore = FALSE). In examples run_multicore is set to; (run_multicore = FALSE).

Information messages were still written to the console which is replaced with the if(verbose)cat(..) option for interactive scripts where printing text to the console is important text is added to the examples and arguments of text indicating that functionality is reduced if verbose is set to FALSE meaning that only basic functionality is maintained

package names, software names and API are now written in quotes e.g. ‘—-’.

some plotting functions opened new windows for new plots, these plot would not show up in Rmarkdown documents. An option was added to turn off the open plots in new windows.

added support for more color palette options. added support to switch the x and y-axis when plotting.

CRAN feedback to version 0.3.0

Please always write package names, software names and API (application programming interface) names in single quotes in title and description. e.g: –> ‘WaverideR’ Please note that package names are case sensitive.

You still have example wrapped within dontrun{} which I think is not necessary. Please unwrap the examples if they are executable in < 5 sec, or replace dontrun{} with donttest{} or explain why dontrun{} is necessary for these examples.

You still write information messages to the console that cannot be easily suppressed. It is more R like to generate objects that can be used to extract the information a user is interested in, and then print() that object. Instead of print()/cat() rather use message()/warning() or if(verbose)cat(..) (or maybe stop()) if you really have to write text to the console. (except for print, summary, interactive functions)

Please confirm that you do not use more than 2 cores in your examples, vignettes, etc.

Changes in version 0.3.0

General changes:

  • Added References both in the description file of the package and the description texts of individual functions.

  • Changed print() statements to if(verbose)cat(..) to allow suppression of messages in the console An exception was made for the astro_anchor function where cat() is used instead because because “feedback” needs to entered into the console

  • spell-checked code and removed misspelled words

  • Removed dontrun from examples and replaced with donttest when examples are executed in >5 seconds otherwise dontrun is removed and extra code is added. Many examples still have donttest added to them as the examples of functions use real-world examples of already published records. Using real-world example data-sets is preferred over synthetic data sets as

  • Previous iterations of functions often contained code which changed the user’s options. by adding oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE) followed by on.exit(par(oldpar)) to functions this issue is avoided. This however makes images/plots uneditable after plotting. To keep images/plot editable the parameter “keep_editable” is added to functions which generate images/plots, If keep_editable is set to TRUE plot/images remain editable but by default keep_editable is set to FALSE to avoid changing the user’s options.

  • Functions which have the option to run on multiple cores have the parameter “run_multicore” added to them. On default run_multicore is set to FALSE to avoid running the process on multiple cores overloading the user’s computer. In all examples run_multicore is set to FALSE meaning that only 1 core is used when a function is executed.

Function specific changes:

  • added astrosignal_example data set
  • added depth_rank_example data set
  • added extract_amplitude function
  • added flmw function function
  • added lithlog_disc function
  • added plot_sed_model function
  • added plot_win_fft function
  • added win_fft function
  • major revision of the max_detect and min_detect functions which reduced the possibility of generating erroneous output

WaverideR 0.2.0

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
